clocks.title: How long things last
clocks.caption: Each dot is a world, read over the last 500 games of its run. A token on a node: how many games a token stays on the node it is on, on average, from the share of all tokens staked at home. A brain on a node: how many games a node goes, on average, before a neighbour takes it and its brain is copied in. An agent: how long an agent lives, the agents alive over the newcomers a game (no dot for the frozen world, in which nobody is born or dies). A group of the flow: of the flow modules of the last 50 games, the life that one in a hundred reaches or passes (50 at most, the games followed). The best-connected place: the longest run of games in which the best-connected agent stayed the same or was a child of the one before (500 at most). B1: five worlds of B1 at 100,000 tokens; B1 star: its largest star; round 3: the five healthiest worlds of round 3; frozen: a world whose brains never change.
clocks.recipe:
**Runs.** Twelve worlds, each read over the last 500 games of its run. Five worlds of B1 at 100,000 tokens (Experiment 10: `B1-100000-s001`, `B1-100000-s003`, `B1-100000-s004`, `B1-100000-s005` and `B1-100000-s006`, the first five seeds whose world is not held together by one hub) and its largest star (`B1-100000-s028`), iterations 1,000 to 1,499. The five healthiest worlds of round 3 by the product ([Which worlds are healthy?](which-worlds-are-healthy.md); Experiments 40 and 42: `B1-30000-b82ad0-s3042`, `B1-30000-8526cf-s4006`, `B1-30000-af1e28-s3018`, `B1-30000-625bc7-s3080` and `B1-30000-38aee9-s3057`), 30,000 tokens, iterations 2,500 to 2,999. And a world whose brains never change and which froze long before its end (Experiment 7, `B1-10000-a8525d-s002`), iterations 2,500 to 2,999.

**Data.** From each run's frames, read once by `particles_pass` in `book_chapters/particles.py` (every game's `decisions.allocations` and `decisions.winners`, and the agents, tokens, connections and parents after it) and kept in `GraphOfLifeRuns/.book/<run>.particles.json`.

1. A token: 1/(1 − h), with h the share of all tokens staked in the games that went to the staker's own node.
2. A brain: the nodes on which anyone staked over those taken by a neighbour.
3. An agent: the mean number of agents after a game over the mean number that were not alive after the game before (Little's law).
4. A group: flow modules followed as on [Flow modules](flow-modules.md#following-groups-through-time) (web/js/flowmodules.js through tools/flowmodules_cli.js); the 99th percentile of their lives.
5. A place: after every game the agent with the most connections; a dynasty goes on while the next one is the same agent or its child.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py particles`.

rings.title: Do tokens go round the same loops?
rings.caption: The net flow of a stretch of games (what each connection carried one way, minus what came back) is split into a part that runs downhill and a part that goes round loops, the circulation. Left: the correlation of the circulation of one stretch with that of the next, over the connections both used; a ring that lasts gives two stretches the same circulation, and a correlation near 1. Each line is a world (orange: B1; red: its largest star; green: round 3; violet: the frozen world, whose circulation turns round every game, and whose net flow over any even number of games is nothing at all). Grey: the median of the eleven worlds that are not frozen, with rings planted on triangles and squares of the connections both stretches used, the same rings in both, carrying 5% or 20% of the circulation there. Right: the same for the downhill part. A swing of the flow back and forth from one game to the next shows at one game, below 0, and cancels in the stretches of an even number of games.
rings.recipe:
**Runs.** Twelve worlds, each read over the last 500 games of its run. Five worlds of B1 at 100,000 tokens (Experiment 10: `B1-100000-s001`, `B1-100000-s003`, `B1-100000-s004`, `B1-100000-s005` and `B1-100000-s006`, the first five seeds whose world is not held together by one hub) and its largest star (`B1-100000-s028`), iterations 1,000 to 1,499. The five healthiest worlds of round 3 by the product ([Which worlds are healthy?](which-worlds-are-healthy.md); Experiments 40 and 42: `B1-30000-b82ad0-s3042`, `B1-30000-8526cf-s4006`, `B1-30000-af1e28-s3018`, `B1-30000-625bc7-s3080` and `B1-30000-38aee9-s3057`), 30,000 tokens, iterations 2,500 to 2,999. And a world whose brains never change and which froze long before its end (Experiment 7, `B1-10000-a8525d-s002`), iterations 2,500 to 2,999.

**Data.** From each run's frames, read once by `particles_pass` in `book_chapters/particles.py` (every game's `decisions.allocations` and `decisions.winners`, and the agents, tokens, connections and parents after it) and kept in `GraphOfLifeRuns/.book/<run>.particles.json`.

1. For every game, the tokens each agent staked on each neighbour's node.
2. Add them up over stretches of 1, 2, 10 and 50 games, one way minus the other: the net flow of each connection (from the first game read, at most 101 stretches in a row).
3. Find the potential that explains as much of the net flow as possible as running downhill (least squares, by conjugate gradients on the network's Laplacian, after pruning dead-end branches, on which no flow goes round); the circulation is the rest ([Flows that go round](measuring-tokens.md#flows-that-go-round)).
4. Correlate each stretch's circulation, and its downhill part, with the next stretch's, over the connections both used; take the median over the pairs of stretches.
5. Positive control: on the connections two stretches share, loops of three or four connections running along 2% of them, each connection used once; the same ring on each loop in both stretches, as strong as makes the rings carry 5% or 20% of the first stretch's circulation on those connections (sum of squares); the same correlation. Rings that last, and nothing else, would give about 0.05 and 0.17.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py particles`.

beats.title: Does anything keep a rhythm?
beats.caption: Top: the spectrum of agents' tokens, game by game, divided by the spectrum of a random walk with the same two memories, one slow and one that swings back and forth, fitted to each stretch; averaged over all the stretches of a world, at periods from two games to half a stretch (anything slower is a trend inside the stretch). Flat means no rhythm beyond the random walk's. Each line is a world (orange: B1; red: its largest star; green: the round-3 worlds with at least 100 stretches). Dashed grey: the same with a weak beat of 5 games planted in every stretch, carrying a sixteenth of its variance (the median of the worlds). Bottom left: the share of stretches with a peak, at a period from 3 games to half the stretch, that a random walk makes less than once in a hundred; at 0, the real stretches; further right, with a beat of a random period planted in each, carrying that share of its variance (the median of the worlds). Bottom right: the swing memory of agents' tokens, by their connections: how much of a swing is left a game later, with its sign (stretches of 128 games; 32 in round 3, drawn a little to the right); one dot per world and class, the median. Dashed: what the even split leaves of a swing between a hub and its leaves alone; below the dotted line, a swing that lasts longer than any such hub's.
beats.recipe:
**Runs.** Twelve worlds, each read over the last 500 games of its run. Five worlds of B1 at 100,000 tokens (Experiment 10: `B1-100000-s001`, `B1-100000-s003`, `B1-100000-s004`, `B1-100000-s005` and `B1-100000-s006`, the first five seeds whose world is not held together by one hub) and its largest star (`B1-100000-s028`), iterations 1,000 to 1,499. The five healthiest worlds of round 3 by the product ([Which worlds are healthy?](which-worlds-are-healthy.md); Experiments 40 and 42: `B1-30000-b82ad0-s3042`, `B1-30000-8526cf-s4006`, `B1-30000-af1e28-s3018`, `B1-30000-625bc7-s3080` and `B1-30000-38aee9-s3057`), 30,000 tokens, iterations 2,500 to 2,999. And a world whose brains never change and which froze long before its end (Experiment 7, `B1-10000-a8525d-s002`), iterations 2,500 to 2,999.

**Data.** From each run's frames, read once by `particles_pass` in `book_chapters/particles.py` (every game's `decisions.allocations` and `decisions.winners`, and the agents, tokens, connections and parents after it) and kept in `GraphOfLifeRuns/.book/<run>.particles.json`.

1. For every agent, its tokens after every game it was alive in the games read.
2. Cut each agent's life into stretches of 32 and of 128 games, back to back; leave out the stretches in which its tokens never change.
3. For each stretch, its correlations with itself one and two games on, r1 and r2; the AR(2) process they give (Yule and Walker), with real roots a ≥ b, the slow memory and the swing memory (where the roots would be complex, the nearest pair of equal real roots); its spectrum σ² / (|1 − a e^(−2πif)|² |1 − b e^(−2πif)|²), scaled to the stretch's variance; and the periodogram, on a grid 4 times finer than the stretch's own frequencies.
4. Chance: 200,000 random walks of each length with two memories drawn from −0.95 to 0.95, fitted the same way; in each bin of the two fitted memories, the highest ratio of periodogram to spectrum, at periods from 3 games to half the stretch, that one in a hundred reaches. A real stretch whose highest ratio is above it is flagged.
5. Positive controls: a sine of a period drawn between 3 games and half the stretch, at a random phase, added to every stretch with the share 1/16, 1/4, 9/16 or 1 of its variance, and the stretches flagged again; and a sine of 5 games with 1/16 of the variance added to every stretch, averaged as the real ones.
6. The two-game swing: a swing memory b below −1/2 − 2.5/√S. Its chance: 20,000 random walks with slow memory 0.85, 0.5 or 0 and swing memory −1/2, and with 0.85 and −2/3, fitted the same way, and the share of them below the line.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py particles`.

groups.title: Groups that last
groups.caption: Of all the flow modules of the last 50 games of each world, the share followed for at least so many games (the median of each kind's worlds; logarithmic axes, a share of 0 drawn at the bottom). The flow: as it was. Partners dealt: the same games with every agent's stakes on its neighbours dealt among the same neighbours at random, which keeps the network and undoes the agents' choice of whom to stake on. Members dealt: the real modules with their agents dealt among them at random, game by game, which keeps only their sizes. B1: five worlds of B1 at 100,000 tokens; B1 star: its largest star; round 3: the five healthiest worlds of round 3; frozen: a world whose brains never change, the positive control, whose modules all last.
groups.recipe:
**Runs.** Twelve worlds, each read over the last 500 games of its run. Five worlds of B1 at 100,000 tokens (Experiment 10: `B1-100000-s001`, `B1-100000-s003`, `B1-100000-s004`, `B1-100000-s005` and `B1-100000-s006`, the first five seeds whose world is not held together by one hub) and its largest star (`B1-100000-s028`), iterations 1,000 to 1,499. The five healthiest worlds of round 3 by the product ([Which worlds are healthy?](which-worlds-are-healthy.md); Experiments 40 and 42: `B1-30000-b82ad0-s3042`, `B1-30000-8526cf-s4006`, `B1-30000-af1e28-s3018`, `B1-30000-625bc7-s3080` and `B1-30000-38aee9-s3057`), 30,000 tokens, iterations 2,500 to 2,999. And a world whose brains never change and which froze long before its end (Experiment 7, `B1-10000-a8525d-s002`), iterations 2,500 to 2,999.

**Data.** From each run's frames, read once by `particles_pass` in `book_chapters/particles.py` (every game's `decisions.allocations` and `decisions.winners`, and the agents, tokens, connections and parents after it) and kept in `GraphOfLifeRuns/.book/<run>.particles.json`.

1. For each of the last 50 games, the flow between each pair of neighbours: the tokens staked either way.
2. Group the agents by the map equation (web/js/flowmodules.js, through tools/flowmodules_cli.js) and follow the groups from game to game: best overlap first, each used once, none below 0.3 of the members two modules share ([Flow modules](flow-modules.md#following-groups-through-time)).
3. Do the same with every agent's stakes on its neighbours dealt among them at random (`--neighbours 1`) and with each game's agents dealt among modules of its sizes (`--shuffle 1`).
4. The share of modules followed for at least so many games; the median of each kind's worlds.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py particles`.

drift.title: Groups that outlast their members, and whether they move
drift.caption: Of the flow modules of the last 50 games followed for 10 games or more, in each world (the worlds' short names; B1 at 100,000 tokens, its star s28, the five round-3 worlds, and the frozen world). Top: the share whose members at the end included none of those it began with. Bottom: how far its last members stood from its first when it began, in steps through the network of its first game; a member born since stands where its nearest forebear alive then stood; the median over the last members, averaged over the modules. Coloured: the flow as it was; grey: with every agent's partners dealt at random among its neighbours, the network's own regions.
drift.recipe:
**Runs.** Twelve worlds, each read over the last 500 games of its run. Five worlds of B1 at 100,000 tokens (Experiment 10: `B1-100000-s001`, `B1-100000-s003`, `B1-100000-s004`, `B1-100000-s005` and `B1-100000-s006`, the first five seeds whose world is not held together by one hub) and its largest star (`B1-100000-s028`), iterations 1,000 to 1,499. The five healthiest worlds of round 3 by the product ([Which worlds are healthy?](which-worlds-are-healthy.md); Experiments 40 and 42: `B1-30000-b82ad0-s3042`, `B1-30000-8526cf-s4006`, `B1-30000-af1e28-s3018`, `B1-30000-625bc7-s3080` and `B1-30000-38aee9-s3057`), 30,000 tokens, iterations 2,500 to 2,999. And a world whose brains never change and which froze long before its end (Experiment 7, `B1-10000-a8525d-s002`), iterations 2,500 to 2,999.

**Data.** From each run's frames, read once by `particles_pass` in `book_chapters/particles.py` (every game's `decisions.allocations` and `decisions.winners`, and the agents, tokens, connections and parents after it) and kept in `GraphOfLifeRuns/.book/<run>.particles.json`.

1. Follow the flow modules of the last 50 games as for the figure above, the real ones and those of the flow with partners dealt.
2. For every module followed 10 games or more: its members in the first game and in the last.
3. Renewed: none of the first members is among the last.
4. Moved: each last member, or its nearest forebear that was alive in the module's first game (parents from the frames' `parent_ids`); its steps to the nearest first member on the network that game's stakes ran on; the median over the last members; the mean over the modules.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py particles`.
